fitoutDecisionPressures.timePressure: Lease start date creates a hard deadline. Furniture not arriving creates real business disruption — staff can't work. This legitimate urgency should be acknowledged and managed proactively.
fitoutDecisionPressures.budgetPressure: Fit-out budget is often set before proper product research. It is frequently under-estimated. TCD's job is to show what the budget will and won't achieve — not to pretend constraints don't exist.
fitoutDecisionPressures.qualityPressure: The client's own clients, partners, and staff will see and work in this space for 5–10 years. Getting it wrong has lasting reputational and productivity consequences.
fitoutDecisionPressures.approvalPressure: Most corporate furniture purchases require committee approval. The internal champion is under pressure to present a compelling case. Give them the tools to succeed.

builderRelationshipImpact.builderDelays: The most common cause of furniture project delay. Always build a 1-week buffer into timelines for builder delays. Communicate this as professional planning, not pessimism.
builderRelationshipImpact.builderMeetings: On large projects, offer to attend a builder coordination meeting — this signals TCD is a professional trade partner, not just a furniture supplier.
builderRelationshipImpact.pcDateUncertainty: Never lock in a firm installation date more than 3 weeks before PC — builders always run late. Confirm delivery within 5 business days of confirmed PC.

relocatingClientPsychology.excitement: New office = new chapter. Clients are emotionally invested in getting it right. Aspirational purchases are justified by the fresh start narrative.
relocatingClientPsychology.anxiety: New office = many moving parts. Anything that adds to their to-do list will feel threatening. Position TCD as reducing complexity, not adding to it.
relocatingClientPsychology.keyMessage: We manage the furniture side so you can focus on your business. One contact, clear timeline, single delivery, professional installation — done.

decisionTimingPsychology.earlyDeciders: Clients who decide on furniture early (6+ months before move) have more time, more options, and higher budgets. Target them with aspirational product positioning.
decisionTimingPsychology.lateDeciders: Clients who decide late (under 8 weeks before move) are under pressure and may accept higher prices for certainty of delivery. Lead with availability and fast-track capability.
decisionTimingPsychology.delayingClients: Clients who keep delaying often have an internal approval problem, not a supplier preference. Ask who else needs to sign off and offer to help with internal presentation.
